name: Tam Coc food guide
summary: Tam Coc eats cơm cháy, mountain goat, and nem Yên Mạc in the hamlet, plus mountain snail and a cook-it-yourself meal at Hang Bụt. The 3 August 2026 family day also names cá rô Tổng Trường at midday. Fourteen plates are named. Six short of twenty. Still not named: a breakfast dish, a sweet, a drink, a noodle, a second rice, a sausage, and a hotpot as its own Tam Coc plate.
body: This is the boat village, not the Ninh Bình city list. DulichToday, updated 25 January 2024, puts cơm cháy with thịt dê núi and tim cật at restaurants in Tam Coc, and names dê nướng and five ốc núi plates. The 20 December 2016 tourism note still describes Ninh Bình cơm cháy with beef, pork heart and kidney, tomato, carrot, onion, and nấm hương. The 20 October 2023 culture office places that beef plate, and the goat cooking, in thành phố Ninh Bình or the old capital. Beef and shiitake stay. Goat and ruốc stay. Both placements stay.

The 23 May 2023 tourism-center note says lunch is inside the Tam Coc tourist area or nearby, and names cơm cháy, dê núi, and nem Yên Mạc. The 14 May 2025 Tam Coc day names dê tái chanh, cơm cháy, and dê nướng at 11:45, with no restaurant and no street. Nem Yên Mạc stays a Yên Mạc plate and a Yên Mô plate as well as that lunch name. No street is named. A plate price is Check on arrival.

The tourism center’s family day, updated 3 August 2026, names cá rô Tổng Trường with dê núi and cơm cháy at midday in Tam Coc, and calls it a Ninh Bình specialty. No restaurant is named. Sở Du lịch Ninh Bình, 23 August 2021, places the fish at Tổng Trường, the old name of xã Trường Yên in Hoa Lư, and names rang, rán, kho, and canh chua, and does not name Tam Coc. The 20 October 2023 culture office places it in the city or the old capital. The 12 February 2026 Tet note says kho tộ or rán giòn on a Ninh Bình Tet table. All of those sentences stay.

Fourteen plates are named. Six short of twenty. Still not named for Tam Coc: a breakfast dish, a sweet, a drink, a noodle, a second rice, a sausage, and a hotpot as its own Tam Coc plate. A provincial goat list of about more than 20 plates does not mention Tam Coc, so it is not copied here. The tourism center’s goat note of 5 June 2026 names dê hấp, dê áp chảo, dê xào sả ớt, dê hầm thuốc bắc, and nem dê, and names Tam Coc only beside Tràng An and Hoa Lư as scenery. Sở Du lịch’s ốc núi page of 24 August 2021 names xào tỏi, xào sa tế, luộc sả, and xào sả ớt, and places that snail in Tam Điệp, Yên Mô, and Nho Quan. The English tourism-center note of 30 July 2021 still names goat soup, grilled goat with five spices, steamed goat with ginger, goat hotpot, and goat porridge, and prints no Vietnamese name. Miến lươn, nem dê, tiết canh dê, lẩu dê, and dê xào lăn stay with the city or the old capital. Kim Sơn, Gia Viễn, and the other Yên Mô plates stay where they were named.
specialtiesLead: Cơm cháy is the crisp rice. Goat, nem Yên Mạc, mountain snail, the Hang Bụt meal, and cá rô Tổng Trường follow.

sections.heading: Tam Coc specialties
paragraphs: Each line is one plate. Cơm cháy, dê tái chanh, nem Yên Mạc, and cá rô Tổng Trường keep the Ninh Bình sentences and the Tam Coc sentences together. The ốc núi plates are April to August on the DulichToday note. Cá rô nướng, canh cua, and cà muối are the Hang Bụt meal, 1 km from chùa Bích Động on one sentence and in Sơn Hà on the next.

Fourteen plates are named. Six short of twenty. Still not named for Tam Coc: a breakfast dish, a sweet, a drink, a noodle, a second rice, a sausage, and a hotpot as its own Tam Coc plate. Hours and a plate price are Check on arrival.
